data.title: North Korea fires ballistic missile after Seoul's apology demand
data.description: SEOUL - North Korea fired a ballistic missile, Seoul's military said Saturday, days after demanding an apology for a blast that wounded three South Korean soldiers in the DMZ that it blames on the North.

data.title: China a better influence in Latin America than US: poll
data.description: BOGOTá - China's influence in Latin America is now viewed more positively than that of the United States, a major poll conducted in 17 Latin American countries showed Friday.

data.title: US regulator finds Boeing 737 MAX software bug 'not a safety concern'
data.description: NEW YORK - A software bug that delayed the US certification of Boeing's 737 MAX 10 aircraft does not pose a safety concern, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said Friday after an investigation.

data.title: Cornell rape case exposes sexual violence at US colleges
data.description: NEW YORK - An alleged gang rape at Cornell University, detailed in a graphic lawsuit last month, has provoked fury in the United States over sexual violence on campuses and colleges' failure to stamp out the behavior.

data.title: New rallies urged in France as protests disrupt 730 schools
data.description: PARIS - French high school students on Friday lit fires and hurled projectiles at police who responded by firing tear gas, as activists urged new rallies in an escalating protest movement demanding better conditions in education.

data.title: Brazil election debate chaos sparks censorship row
data.description: RIO DE JANEIRO (BRAZIL) - Brazil's judiciary came under fire Friday for sparking the cancellation of an election debate by meddling in its rules after President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva refused to attend.

data.title: Argentina unveils passports-for-investment scheme
data.description: BUENOS AIRES (ARGENTINA) - Argentine President Javier Milei's government said Friday that the country would offer citizenship to foreigners who invest at least $350,000 in the country.

data.title: King Charles to evoke colonial 'darkest days' on Caribbean tour
data.description: LONDON - King Charles III will acknowledge the "darkest days" of colonial rule and slavery while touring Caribbean countries on a visit beginning this month, a Buckingham Palace spokesperson said Friday.

data.title: Russia ‘tearing Kyiv apart’, mayor says
data.description: KYIV - Russian attacks on key infrastructure were “tearing Kyiv apart”, the city’s mayor said Friday, as strikes on a bridge linking the capital’s east and west brought traffic to a standstill.

data.title: China widens military footprint with Laos air base
data.description: BANGKOK - When China opened its first overseas air force base this week, a joint facility in isolated Laos, it was sending a signal — its foreign military foothold is set to grow, analysts say.

data.title: Tigray conflict puts Ethiopia at odds with neighbours
data.description: ADDIS ABABA - Ethiopia’s Tigray rebels have been pushed out of a neighbouring state by a government counter-offensive, a humanitarian source said Friday, but the conflict has triggered a breakdown in the country’s relations with Eritrea and Egypt.

data.title: Swiss president to quit government
data.description: GENEVA - Swiss President Guy Parmelin announced on Friday that he will quit the government at the end of the year, in a sudden move after more than a decade of ministerial service.

data.title: WHO: Life expectancy almost back to pre-Covid levels
data.description: GENEVA - Global life expectancy is close to the levels seen before the Covid-19 pandemic, but the outlook for years lived in good health is recovering more slowly, the World Health Organization said on Friday.

data.title: Spain housing reform vote pending as protests mount
data.description: MADRID - Spain’s parliament was to vote Friday on government housing decrees introduced after nationwide protests triggered by the eviction of an 87-year-old woman, but there were doubts the measures would pass.

data.title: Swedish Social Democrats try again to form government
data.description: STOCKHOLM - Sweden’s parliament speaker said on Friday that he had asked Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson to make a new attempt to form a government, days after a first bid failed.

data.title: Flydubai pilot opened cockpit door to save passengers
data.description: DUBAI - An Indian pilot attacked by his co-pilot aboard a flight from the UAE to Israel said on Friday that he “could not let all those people die”, in his first public remarks after he helped stop the plane from crashing.

data.title: North Korean leader’s sister calls Seoul ‘despicable’
data.description: SEOUL - Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of North Korea’s leader, called South Korea “despicable” Friday after Seoul demanded an apology over an explosion in the Demilitarised Zone that wounded three of its soldiers.

data.title: Indian flydubai pilot opened cockpit door to save passengers
data.description: NEW DELHI — Indian flydubai captain Smit Machchhar knew he had to act quickly after an alleged in-flight attack by his co-pilot, opening the cockpit door in a "last push" to get help and avert disaster, he said Friday.

data.title: Macron urges G7 coordination as US presses Europe on diesel stocks
data.description: BRUSSELS (BELGIUM) - French leader Emmanuel Macron urged G7 nations to work together to bring down fuel prices in a call with President Donald Trump on Friday, as Washington pressures Europe to tap its strategic diesel reserves and threatens curbs on US exports.

data.title: World powers gather in Pacific to chart climate battle
data.description: WELLINGTON - World powers are flying delegates to the Pacific to haggle over the fight against global warming, and to see the plight of island nations surrounded by a rising ocean.

data.title: Taiwan receives its first US-made F-16V fighter jets
data.description: TAITUNG (TAIWAN) - Taiwan received on Friday its first F-16V fighter jets made by the United States, as the island democracy upgrades its military capabilities to deter a potential Chinese attack.

data.title: Lula, Bolsonaro trade scandal fire in final scramble for votes
data.description: BRASíLIA - Brazil's President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and his election rival Flavio Bolsonaro are leaving no controversy unturned in their last-ditch efforts to discredit each other and win over voters ahead of Sunday's nail-biter election.

data.title: Return of swarming moth spectacle has Australia in a flutter
data.description: SYDNEY - Moth swarms so thick they can blot out the stars are fluttering across Australia, heralding a migratory spectacle unseen since the creature's brush with extinction nearly 10 years ago.

data.title: Nepal's grim DNA puzzle to identify flood dead
data.description: NUWAKOT (NEPAL) - Clutching a photograph of his missing son, Rajesh Ram is pinning his hopes on deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) testing -- like thousands of others desperately seeking relatives swept away by Nepal's catastrophic Himalayan floods.

data.title: Arab Israeli candidate drops out of election race
data.description: JERUSALEM — Arab Israeli politician Sami Abu Shehadeh withdrew his candidacy on Thursday from October's parliamentary election after Israel's Supreme Court indicated a majority of its judges supported barring him from the race.

data.title: Viral anti-vax posts weaponise Philippine inoculation fears
data.description: MANILA - When Jenette Torres Odena's three-year-old son fell ill days after receiving a jab as part of a Philippine vaccination drive, his photograph quickly spread on Facebook alongside claims the inoculation had killed him.

data.title: Israel courts Europe's far right, finding friends but also unease
data.description: JERUSALEM - Facing growing isolation over the war in Gaza, Israel is increasingly allying itself with Europe's far right, despite some parties' legacies of antisemitism.

data.title: Saudi coalition accuses Houthis of drone attack on Medina
data.description: RIYADH (SAUDI ARABIA) - Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis struck an electricity distribution station in the holy city of Medina in Saudi Arabia, the Saudi-led coalition said on Thursday, sparking strong condemnation from the Muslim world.

data.title: US says 'in Europe's best interest' to cooperate on fuel supply
data.description: MILWAUKEE - The United States told Europe on Thursday to cooperate with Washington's efforts to lower diesel prices, while a top EU official said a US export ban of the fuel would be "unexpected."

data.title: A saintly spat and debate snub: Brazil enters final polls stretch
data.description: BRASíLIA - Brazil's electoral court has ordered the takedown of "untrue" social media posts about the country's patron saint, the latest row at the end of a deeply divisive election campaign that will see President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva snub the main debate on Thursday.

data.title: Trump vows to hit Iran 'very hard' if linked to flydubai attack
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump said Thursday that Tehran was likely involved in an attack by a pilot on a flydubai flight to Israel and that Iran would be "hit very hard" if it was.

data.title: Ethiopia and Eritrea break diplomatic ties over conflict
data.description: ADDIS ABABA - Ethiopia and Eritrea broke diplomatic ties on Thursday, accusing each other of stoking internal conflicts as fighting continued in northern Ethiopia.

data.title: Libya's pay strike rallies teachers across divided nation
data.description: TRIPOLI - In Libya, a teachers' strike over pay has shut schools and delayed the start of the school year, rallying educators across the oil-rich but politically divided country.

data.title: How airlines try to make sure pilots are safe to fly
data.description: PARIS (FRANCE) - The apparent attack by the co-pilot on a flight to Israel, in which he stabbed his captain and tried to crash the plane, is a reminder that the cockpit is an extremely sensitive place in terms of aviation safety.

data.title: Family of woman killed by US immigration agent sues Trump administration
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The family of Renee Good, an unarmed US citizen shot dead by an immigration agent during a sweeping federal crackdown, sued President Donald Trump's administration on Thursday, alleging wrongful death and civil rights violations.
